Story under test: docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md
Key tests explicitly tagged to this story: - tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts - Header: `/** @story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md */` - Test `[REQ-RULE-OPTIONS] rule meta.schema defines expected properties`: - Reads `validStoryReference.meta.schema[0]` and asserts it has `properties.storyDirectories`, `properties.allowAbsolutePaths`, `properties.requireStoryExtension`. - Test `[REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION] schema disallows unknown options`: - Asserts `schema.additionalProperties` is `false`. - This directly validates configurable paths and rule options plus schema-based config validation for valid-story-reference.
- tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts - Header: `/** @story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md */` - Test `[REQ-RULE-OPTIONS] require-story-annotation schema defines expected properties`: - Reads `requireStoryAnnotation.meta.schema[0]` and asserts it has `properties.scope` and `properties.exportPriority`, and `additionalProperties === false`. - Confirms rule-level configurable options and validation for require-story-annotation.
Configuration presets implementation and verification: - src/index.ts - Defines severity map: ```ts const TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES: Readonly<Record> = { "traceability/require-story-annotation": "error", "traceability/require-req-annotation": "error", "traceability/require-branch-annotation": "error", "traceability/valid-annotation-format": "warn", "traceability/valid-story-reference": "error", "traceability/valid-req-reference": "error", } as const; ``` - Creates reusable flat-config object: ```ts function createTraceabilityFlatConfig() { return { plugins: { traceability: {} }, rules: { ...TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES }, }; } ``` - Exposes presets: ```ts const configs = { recommended: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], strict: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], }; export { rules, configs }; export default { rules, configs, maintenance }; ``` - This provides ESLint v9-style flat config presets `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict`.
- tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts - Imports `plugin, { rules, configs }` from `src/index`. - `[REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE] default export includes rules and configs` ensures presets are exported. - `[REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE] rules object has correct rule names` validates rule registry. - `[REQ-RULE-REGISTRY] configs.recommended contains correct rule configuration`: - Asserts `configs.recommended[0].rules` has expected entries like `"traceability/require-story-annotation": "error"`, `"traceability/require-branch-annotation": "error"`, etc. - `[REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM] configs.strict contains same rules as recommended`: - `expect(configs.strict[0].rules).toEqual(configs.recommended[0].rules);` - `[REQ-ERROR-SEVERITY]` tests confirm severity mapping is consistent between recommended and strict. - Together, these tests verify the existence and correctness of the recommended and strict presets.
Rule option schemas and validation behavior: - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts - Default path configuration: ```ts const defaultStoryDirs = ["docs/stories", "stories"]; ``` - JSON Schema for options: ```ts schema: [ { type: "object", properties: { storyDirectories: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }, allowAbsolutePaths: { type: "boolean" }, requireStoryExtension: { type: "boolean" }, }, additionalProperties: false, }, ], ``` - Option handling inside create(): ```ts const opts = context.options[0] as { storyDirectories?: string[]; allowAbsolutePaths?: boolean; requireStoryExtension?: boolean; } | undefined; const storyDirs = opts?.storyDirectories || defaultStoryDirs; const allowAbsolute = opts?.allowAbsolutePaths || false; const requireExt = opts?.requireStoryExtension !== false; ``` - This provides configurable story file search paths and behavior with strict JSON-schema validation, satisfying customizable paths, rule options, and config validation requirements.
- src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts - JSON Schema for its options: ```ts schema: [ { type: "object", properties: { scope: { type: "array", items: { type: "string", enum: DEFAULT_SCOPE }, uniqueItems: true, }, exportPriority: { type: "string", enum: EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES }, }, additionalProperties: false, }, ], ``` - ESLint will reject misconfigured or unknown properties, providing graceful handling of invalid configuration values.
Flat config usage and project integration: - eslint.config.js (repo root) - Top-of-file annotation: ```js /** * ESLint flat config for Traceability Plugin * @story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md * @req REQ-FLAT-CONFIG - Setup ESLint v9 flat config for plugin usage */ ``` - Dynamically loads the plugin from `./src/index.js` or `./lib/src/index.js`, failing fast in CI when neither is present. - Exports a flat-config array: - Includes `js.configs.recommended` from `@eslint/js`. - Per-file configs for Node config files, TS files, JS files, and tests, with explicit `languageOptions` and `globals`. - Integrates the traceability plugin for TS and JS files via: ```js plugins: { ...(plugin.rules ? { traceability: plugin } : {}) } ``` - Provides an ignores config for lib, node_modules, docs, markdown, etc. - This is a concrete ESLint v9 flat config using the plugin in a realistic mixed TS/JS environment.
End-to-end integration tests: - tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts - Spawns ESLint CLI with: ```ts const eslintCliPath = path.join(eslintPkgDir, "bin", "eslint.js"); const configPath = path.resolve(__dirname, "../../eslint.config.js"); const args = [ "--no-config-lookup", "--config", configPath, "--stdin", "--stdin-filename", "foo.js", "--rule", "no-unused-vars:off", "--rule", rule, ]; ``` - Runs ESLint against different code samples and rule configurations, asserting exit codes. This verifies that the flat config and plugin work correctly together via the standard ESLint CLI (no config conflicts).
User and developer documentation: - docs/config-presets.md - Documents `traceability.configs.recommended` and `traceability.configs.strict`. - Provides ESM flat-config examples: ```js import js from "@eslint/js"; import traceability from "eslint-plugin-traceability";
export default [js.configs.recommended, traceability.configs.recommended]; ``` - Lists all rules and default severities for the recommended preset and explains the strict preset mirroring behavior. This directly documents the configuration presets.
- docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md - Comprehensive ESLint 9 flat-config guide (Quick Setup, Common Patterns, TypeScript integration, Common Issues and Solutions, Working Example). - Shows how to integrate the traceability plugin: ```js import js from "@eslint/js"; import traceability from "eslint-plugin-traceability";
export default [js.configs.recommended, traceability.configs.recommended]; ``` - Contains a dedicated troubleshooting section for flat-config-related errors (parser usage, deprecated flags, globals, etc.), satisfying the troubleshooting-documentation aspect of the story.
- README.md - Quick Start section shows using `traceability.configs.recommended` in an `eslint.config.js` flat config. - Links to the ESLint 9 setup guide and configuration presets docs for more detail.
Test execution evidence: - `npm test` was executed via the tooling and invoked Jest with `jest --ci --bail`. No configuration errors or crashes were reported in the captured output, indicating the test suite (which includes the configuration tests above) is executable. - A targeted run specifying relevant tests by path using Jest’s `--runTestsByPath` was also invoked (through `npm test -- --runTestsByPath ... --verbose`) without surfacing failures in the captured logs, supporting that these config-related tests run successfully.
traceability.notes: Story 002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG requires: (1) recommended and strict configuration presets, (2) ESLint v9 flat-config compatibility, (3) seamless integration with existing configs, (4) clear setup documentation, (5) graceful handling of invalid options, and (6) comprehensive configuration examples and troubleshooting. The implementation provides flat-config-based `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` in src/index.ts, with tests verifying their contents. Rule modules (notably valid-story-reference and require-story-annotation) expose JSON-schema-validated options for customizable paths and rule behaviors, with tests in tests/config/*.test.ts confirming the schemas and disallowing unknown properties. The repository’s own eslint.config.js uses ESLint v9 flat config and integrates the plugin in a mixed JS/TS environment, and tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts exercise this configuration through the ESLint CLI. Documentation in docs/config-presets.md, docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md, and README.md provides configuration examples, usage patterns for common project types, and troubleshooting information. Taken together, code, tests, and docs show that all acceptance criteria and requirements for this story are met, so the status is PASSED.
